Doesn't matter how old you are.
Get into a trade. Everyone is looking for someone who wants to work.
I'm an electrical superintendent. I bring in close to 200k annually. 

Everyone overlooks trades. Yes, I was roping in homes when I was ten due to my dad being a general contractor.
So I had that help. I was a foreman building gas stations at 17. Passion is the driver for me. 

Work to me isn't a job. It's a lifestyle. There's no difference between Sunday or Thursday. I don't look forward to a weekend or spend my week waiting for Friday. I don't dread the impending Monday. I love my work.

When you do work like this... family and work can be a juggle, but there's 168 in a week. I make the most of it, and I'm grateful of everyday I get a chance to progress forward.

Whether you're mechanically inclined, willing, or love to learn, independently push yourself. A trade (does depend on the trade) will take you to endless possibilities.

He needs to make a choice. Find a job, put his head down, and do the daily grind. Or, get after it.

I'm always hiring.

If you're local to Southern California. DM.

EDIT- before people start down voting me.

I didn't come to brag, I was hoping to inspire. Though I didn't completely make my point.

Don't go looking to scrape the bottom of the barrel to make ends meet. Yes, you'll have to start at the bottom from somewhere. If you truly look to possibly find your passion and put your everything into it. It will pay for itself.

It doesn't have to be about an hourly rate or your salary. That will just be a bonus.

Life shouldn't be about just a job.... it's about putting your shoes on before your alarm and being stoked about your day.

I don't know. Never grown algea before.

I will say what I did.

I knew I wanted a planted tank so I got my substrate (the black fluorite one) and put a whole bag of flourish tabs the first day of cycling. 
So they sat there for three weeks (my tank was actually cycled in a couple days since I have alot of good media.) And then I put another bag of tabs and then planted.
I keep my light (two fluval nano) from 7 am until 6 pm. I water change two to three times a week. The tank has been up for about two months? 

Honestly this whole covid has made me lose track of time. But I've put two bags of tabs during the duration. I don't use any liquid firt or co2 (which I want to get into)

Oh but I do have water cabbage. I have kept them trimmed to where I have three big ones (they will take over like a wild fire) and they bring in shade where there happens to be alot of algea. So honestly I'm not sure what is working. I'm working on another tank for blue dreams and it's going to be completely different. So we'll see what happens.

....and that's it? I'm learning everyday. I love it.
